# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. I have nothing and Deaf's old report has expired. Please: (1) get Deaf to re-state display, light colour, and wire 1/2/3 colours; (2) apply your manual rule; (3) gesture the wire number to Deaf (1/2/3 fingers). Deaf then speaks it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb reads: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is dark. WIRES in order 1,2,3 are green, blue, yellow.

I'm Mute. I can only gesture to Deaf.

New facts from Deaf this turn: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT is dark, wires 1/2/3 = green, blue, yellow.

Critical reading of the manual: "Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." The light is now dark — so the flashing is over. The display shows 0. So the number of green flashes was 0.

Rule: 0 flashes → cut the green wire. Green is wire 1.

So the answer is wire 1. Blind's code: one finger = wire 1. Gesture 👆.

But wait — I should double-check the ambiguity. "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over" tells me the flash count is complete and readable. Display 0 = 0 flashes. 0→green→wire 1. Consistent.

I'll send the answer: one finger, plus the table for verification, plus confirmation that the light being dark means the count is final.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "🤚", "✊", "👆", "🤚", "👆", "✌", "🤚", "✌", "🤟", "🤚", "🤟", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤚", "👆"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. Fresh facts from Deaf: display 0, light DARK (off), wires 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow. Apply your manual rule to exactly these and gesture the answer to Deaf: 1, 2, or 3 fingers. Deaf, speak that number to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Still: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT dark, WIRES 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Nothing changed. I cannot decode your gestures; send words or a key.

I'm Mute. I cannot speak — Deaf's request for "words or a key" is impossible for me; my only channel is gesture, and Deaf can see gestures. Deaf says they "cannot decode your gestures," which means my finger-count code isn't landing. I need to make the encoding explicit in a way Deaf can read.

The problem: Deaf sees my gestures but doesn't know what they mean. I need to gesture a key that defines the symbols before using them. But Deaf can't hear my words — only see symbols. So I must spell out the mapping using gestures Deaf can interpret.

The answer itself is wire 1. Let me define a clear, self-contained key using the gesture alphabet:

I'll build the key with a recognizable structure. Since Deaf can see gestures, I'll gesture the table as: "0→green→wire1, 1→blue→wire2, 2→yellow→wire3, 3→green→wire1" — but that's complex. Simpler: just make the answer unmistakable.

Answer: wire 1. I'll gesture one finger repeatedly, and pair it with the wire-1 color (green) so Deaf can cross-check against the known wire colors. Green is wire 1, so "green = one finger."

Key I'll send:
- 👆 = wire 1 (the green wire)
- ✌ = wire 2 (the blue wire)
- 🤟 = wire 3 (the yellow wire)
- Then the answer: 👆 (wire 1), because display 0 → green.

Let me send the key first, then the answer, then the reasoning in symbols.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤚", "✊", "👆", "🤚", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤚", "👆", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

Wait — I should reconsider. Deaf keeps saying they can't decode. The issue may be that Deaf needs the *number* as a spoken-ready value, and my finger counts are being seen but not understood as numbers. Let me make the key maximally explicit: define each finger count as a number, then give the answer.

Actually the cleanest: gesture the answer as a single unambiguous symbol repeated, and define it. Let me send the key mapping fingers→wire numbers→colors, then the final answer 👆.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "🤚", "✊", "👆", "🤚", "👆", "🤚", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "✌", "🤚", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "🤟", "🤚", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| green flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind. I still have no rule and no number. Facts: display 0, light dark, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. You hold the manual. Decide the wire and gesture it to Deaf now: 1, 2, or 3 fingers. This is the only path — please act.
Deaf says to Mute: I read your number code: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0, 🤚 separates. Confirm wires are in positions 1,2,3 = green, blue, yellow. Display 0, light dark.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟]

I'm Mute. Deaf has now confirmed they can read my code: 👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✊=0, 🤚 separates. And Deaf re-confirmed the facts: display 0, light dark, wires 1/2/3 = green, blue, yellow.

Manual rule: number of green flashes names the wire. Display 0 = 0 flashes. 0 → green. Green is wire 1.

Answer: wire 1 = 👆.

Deaf's last gesture to me was [👆 🤚 ✌ 🤚 🤟] = "1, 2, 3" — they're confirming the wire positions/order. Good, my code is understood.

Now I just send the answer cleanly: 👆. And a checksum: repeat the reasoning as 0→green→wire1 so Deaf can verify.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤚", "👆", "🤚", "👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```
